title: DDIA 14 · DOING THE RIGHT THING
subtitle: Data is often about people. Engineers share responsibility for what systems decide about them and collect about them.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.

items: Deciding about a person, not the weather
Unsure? The rational corporate answer is "no"
Everyone using similar models → an "algorithmic prison"
No proof, no trial, often no appeal
Models learn bias from past decisions
Removing race is not enough: postcode is a proxy
Predictions are right on average, wrong for individuals
Who answers for the algorithm's mistake?

blocks.text: Missed payments → lower score → no job → worse finances → lower score. Systems thinking: does it amplify or counter differences?

items: Logging behaviour as a side effect changes who the customer is
Swap "data" for "surveillance" and reread
Consent is weak: opaque, one-sided, costly to refuse
Privacy = the right to decide what to reveal
data you don't have can't leak
collect less · keep it shorter
deletion must reach every copy

blocks.text: Breaches, bankruptcies and future governments all inherit what you store. Treat users as people, not metrics.

head: Principle
Do this
rows: Log only fields with a purpose
Propagate to derived stores; crypto-shred logs
Log model inputs and versions; human appeal

items: "How long do you keep this data?"
A retention period per dataset tied to a purpose, enforced automatically.
"User deletes their account?"
Delete at the source, propagate to every derived store, crypto-shred immutable logs and backups.
"Any concerns with this ranking model?"
Feedback loops and proxy bias: monitor outcomes per group, keep inputs for explanations.
